translationRepairs: Wei Can; Jiang Ziyi; his younger nephew Zisi and nephew Ziwu; Zhang Sheng; Shen Jun; Liu Jingli
Wei Can; Jiang Ziyi; his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu; Zhang Sheng; Shen Jun; Liu Jingli
Title line 弟子四 子五 uses 弟 for Jiang Ziyi’s younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu, not nephews; replacing “nephew” with “younger brothers” restores that kinship.
Wei Can; Jiang Ziyi; younger nephew Zisi; nephew Ziwu; Zhang Sheng; Shen Jun; Liu Jingli
Wei Can; Jiang Ziyi; younger brother Zisi; younger brother Ziwu; Zhang Sheng; Shen Jun; Liu Jingli
The same heading marks Zisi and Ziwu with 弟; literal “nephew” is kinship error, and “younger brother” for each matches the Chinese.
His younger nephew Zisi had held gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.
His younger brother Zisi had held gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.
弟子四 introduces Zisi as Ziyi’s younger brother; s0078 兄弟性並剛烈 confirms they are brothers, so “nephew” must become “younger brother.”
His younger nephew Zisi had held the post of gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.
His younger brother Zisi had held the post of gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.
Literal 弟子四 is the kinship formula “younger brother Zisi,” not nephew; the proposed swap alone corrects the error.
He asked with his nephews Zisi and Ziwu to lead more than a hundred men to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the bandit.
He asked with his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu to lead more than a hundred men to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the bandit.
請與其弟子四、子五 means he asks to go with his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu; “nephews” invents the wrong kinship.
He asked with his nephews Zisi and Ziwu to lead their command of more than a hundred men to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the bandit.
He asked with his younger brothers Zisi and Ziwu to lead their command of more than a hundred men to open the Chengming Gate and challenge the bandit.
The same 弟 marks Zisi and Ziwu as younger brothers in the literal field; “younger brothers” is the accurate rendering.
Jing laid a blade across his knee and glared with true eyes and shouted at him.
Jing laid a blade across his knee and glared angrily and shouted at him.

Local 暿真目 is unintelligible and yields “true eyes”; Wikisource preserves the same garble, while CText’s parallel reads toward 目叱之 and the intended idiom is 瞋目 “glare angrily,” so the proposed literal is correct.
Jing laid a blade across his knee and glared and shouted at him.
Jing laid a blade across his knee, glared angrily, and shouted at him.
With the source emended to 瞋目, anger is part of the glare; adding “angrily” aligns the idiomatic with that sense without inventing new content.
